nodes.description: Sporangia embedded in mucosal tissue provoke chronic inflammatory and granulomatous tissue expansion, yielding friable hyperplastic polyps with neutrophils, lymphocytes, plasma cells, fibroblasts, and blood vessels.

evidence.reference_title: Unusual fungal and pseudofungal infections of humans.
evidence.snippet: Rhinosporidiosis is a granulomatous disease of humans and animals that is characterized by the development of mucosal polyps that primarily affect the nasopharynx and ocular conjunctiva of infected individuals

evidence.snippet: Hyperplastic squamous epithelium and oedematous fibro-connective tissue with many globular cysts, fibroblasts, and inflammatory cells such as neutrophils, lymphocytes, and plasma cells are found on histopathological examination.

nodes.description: Treatment centers on complete excision of visible lesions with cauterizing or coblation of the attachment base to remove sporangia and limit local seeding.

nodes.description: Susceptible humans probably acquire infection when R. seeberi endospores from aquatic or marshy environments contact nasal or other mucosal epithelium, especially after local epithelial injury.

evidence.snippet: The presumed mode of infection of R. seeberi is through the epithelium (“transepithelial infection”) most commonly found in nasal sites

nodes.description: Endospores in mucosal tissue activate and mature through trophocyte forms into large sporangia packed with endospores at multiple developmental stages.

Epistaxis and nasal obstruction are the most common findings. It may be unilateral or bilateral. The enlargement of these lesions occurs slowly over months or years.

nodes.description: Nasal rhinosporidiosis usually presents as a slow-growing, friable, reddish, unilateral polypoid mass in the nasal cavity or nasopharynx.

evidence.snippet: The main characteristic of the disease is the occurrence of a polypoidal, reddish, friable, painless, pedunculated, hyperplastic soft tissue mass in the nasal area
